turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Mrs Deshpande, vitals are done. Weight 74 kilos, blood pressure 124 over 78, pulse 64, temperature 36.2, oxygen saturation 98 percent. Doctor is free, you can go in.
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): Come, sit down. I glanced at those numbers, pulse is a little slow, not by itself a panic. What brought you today?

[SEG0003] person_3 (PATIENT): Doctor, the main thing is I am tired all the time, and I feel cold. It has been months. I work in accounts at a textile showroom, I kept saying it is the job and my age, I am forty-eight, and my husband finally said enough, and Geeta, she is our live-in help, she also said I must come.
[SEG0004] person_2 (DOCTOR): Tired and cold, alright. From when, even a rough season is enough, don't force an exact date if you don't have one.

[SEG0005] person_3 (PATIENT): Um, that is the problem, I cannot date it. Since Diwali, or after Diwali, something like that. Last winter, or the one before, I was already carrying a shawl in the accounts room while the others wanted the fan. I have tried to fix the month and I simply cannot.
[SEG0006] person_4 (CAREGIVER): Many months, Doctor, that much I can say. Which winter, I also cannot tell you. She asked me yesterday and I had no answer.
[SEG0007] person_2 (DOCTOR): Then we leave the onset open, no invented date. How does the tiredness actually show in the day?

[SEG0008] person_3 (PATIENT): I wake up dull, as if I did not sleep, even when I did. After lunch, around two, I am finished, I want to put my head on the GST files. I still complete the entries, I don't bunk, but in the evening I cannot even sit for the serial I used to watch daily.
[SEG0009] person_2 (DOCTOR): And the cold, is it only in that office AC or at home also?

[SEG0010] person_3 (PATIENT): Home also. My hands and my feet are cold. I blamed the AC, then I noticed the AC is off on many days and I am still cold, so that theory of mine fell flat. Geeta is in a cotton sari and I am in a sweater, it looks silly.
[SEG0011] person_4 (CAREGIVER): It is true. She tells me to shut the window, I am the one who wants the fan. Afternoon also, sweater.
[SEG0012] person_2 (DOCTOR): Has your weight moved?

[SEG0013] person_3 (PATIENT): I have put on five kilos, no, sorry, that was a loose guess. It is about eight kilos. My salwar waist is tight, and I am not eating more, I actually eat less because cooking feels like a project when I am this tired.
[SEG0014] person_1 (NURSE): Sorry to cut in. Last year's card in the file says 66 kilos. Today I measured 74. I thought you should both see that.
[SEG0015] person_2 (DOCTOR): So eight kilos lines up with 66 to 74, near enough. What about your motions, any constipation?

[SEG0016] person_3 (PATIENT): Yes, and I will over-explain, forgive me. I pass motion once in three days, sometimes four, hard, I have to strain. I take isabgol, I started with two spoons, no, one spoon, at night in warm water. Two spoons bloated me so I corrected it myself to one spoon and that is what I take.
[SEG0017] person_2 (DOCTOR): One spoon at night, got it. Any blood in the stool, or pain in the abdomen that is severe?
[SEG0018] person_3 (PATIENT): No blood. No severe pain. Only the hardness and the three-four day gap. I keep a water bottle and then I forget it exists.
[SEG0019] person_4 (CAREGIVER): One spoon, I see that. Water, she forgets. I nag her.
[SEG0020] person_2 (DOCTOR): You said you stopped enjoying the serial. How is the mood, separate from the tiredness?

[SEG0021] person_3 (PATIENT): Low, not in a filmy way, but flat, and I get irritated and then I feel bad about it. Sometimes I cry in the bathroom so the showroom staff don't notice. I have been blaming the workload and my age. I keep saying I am turning fifty though I am still forty-eight, which is just me rounding it up.
[SEG0022] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any thought of harming yourself, even once, even briefly?
[SEG0023] person_3 (PATIENT): No. Not that. I want my old energy back. I still call my daughter in Pune every evening, that part I have not dropped.
[SEG0024] person_2 (DOCTOR): Hair, skin, swelling of the feet, periods, anything changed there?

[SEG0025] person_3 (PATIENT): Hair fall is more, on the comb, not in clumps. Skin on my arms is dry, I rub coconut oil and it stays dry. Periods are still monthly and they are a bit heavier than before. Feet are not swollen, I looked for sock marks and there are none.
[SEG0026] person_4 (CAREGIVER): Bathroom floor has more hair, I sweep it every day. And she is quiet in the house, dull quiet, not her usual talking.
[SEG0027] person_2 (DOCTOR): In the family, thyroid, sugar, heart, anything?

[SEG0028] person_3 (PATIENT): My mother had thyroid disease, hypothyroidism, the slow one. She took thyroxine for years, I think a hundred micrograms, but that was her tablet, please don't write it as mine. She died three years ago. My father has sugar, diabetes, he is still there, and I am not on any of his tablets.
[SEG0029] person_2 (DOCTOR): And you, was your own thyroid ever tested?

[SEG0030] person_3 (PATIENT): Once. They said borderline. I can hear myself saying that word, borderline, like it is a fact. The lab was near the showroom. Two years back, or three, I cannot date that either, same problem as the shawl.

[SEG0031] person_4 (CAREGIVER): Doctor, I kept the paper in the blue file at home. It did not say borderline. TSH was in the normal range, someone had circled normal. She has repeated borderline so many times she believes it. The paper says normal.

[SEG0032] person_3 (PATIENT): If you read normal, then I have mixed it up, haven't I. My sister-in-law was the borderline one. I was so sure till this minute. The paper is not here, so I cannot prove anything, but I should not insist.

[SEG0033] person_2 (DOCTOR): Then I will not record borderline. What Geeta saw was a normal report, you may have borrowed your sister-in-law's word, and we still don't have the sheet in the room. Your own medicines, what do you actually take?

[SEG0034] person_3 (PATIENT): Vitamin D, the sachet, cholecalciferol, sixty thousand units every week, no, sorry, not weekly. The chemist said weekly and I never followed that, it is once a month. The orthopaedic started it last year for low vitamin D. Whether I took the last sachet last month or the month before, I am honestly not sure.
[SEG0035] person_2 (DOCTOR): So the dose stays sixty thousand units, the timing is monthly, not weekly, and the taking of it is a bit doubtful. Any blood pressure tablet, any thyroxine of your own?

[SEG0036] person_3 (PATIENT): No blood pressure tablet. I have never taken thyroxine. Once I looked at my mother's old strip in the cupboard and I did not swallow it. No drug allergy that I know, no food allergy either.
[SEG0037] person_4 (CAREGIVER): I was there that day, she did not swallow it. The vitamin D box is in the kitchen and I did not tick any date, so I also cannot say the last sachet went in.
[SEG0038] person_2 (DOCTOR): Just to be tidy, any allergy at all, penicillin or otherwise, or none?
[SEG0039] person_3 (PATIENT): None. I had penicillin once for a tooth, years ago, no rash, no swelling, nothing.

[SEG0040] person_2 (DOCTOR): Let me feel the neck. Swallow, please. I am not feeling a lump, the gland is not enlarged. Pulse is regular, same as that 64. Forearms, the skin is dry, mild. Ankles, no swelling.
[SEG0041] person_3 (PATIENT): It did not hurt when you pressed. The dryness is exactly what I meant, oil or no oil.

[SEG0042] person_2 (DOCTOR): I am thinking aloud, tell me if I rush. Tired, cold, about eight kilos up, constipated, low mood, dry skin, more hair fall, mother with hypothyroidism. Work and age can tire a person, I accept that story partly, but this bunch is how an underactive thyroid behaves. I would call it possible hypothyroidism, not a diagnosis, a working impression only.
[SEG0043] person_3 (PATIENT): Even if that old test was normal, if Geeta is right?

[SEG0044] person_2 (DOCTOR): Yes. A normal test from two or three years ago, whichever it was, does not close the question for today. And I am not starting thyroxine on a hunch, because if I treat first I spoil the blood test. Borderline we have already set aside as a wrong memory.
[SEG0045] person_4 (CAREGIVER): Good. She should not start Madam's mother's tablets. I was worried you might say half a tablet.

[SEG0046] person_2 (DOCTOR): Please do not take anybody else's thyroxine. Continue isabgol one spoon at night, and actually drink water, not just carry the bottle. If the mood drops further or you get any thought of harming yourself, come sooner, don't wait for the report.

[SEG0047] person_3 (PATIENT): Water I can do. Isabgol I am already on. The old tablets I will not touch, Geeta can throw the strip if it is even still there, I think it is, or maybe I cleared it, anyway I won't take it.

[SEG0048] person_2 (DOCTOR): For tests, I nearly ticked TSH and T3, but T3 is the wrong one for this question, let me correct myself. I want TSH and free T4, and a haemoglobin, because tiredness can be anaemia as well. No fasting sugar today, your father's diabetes is not a reason to add it this morning.
[SEG0049] person_1 (NURSE): I can draw after the consult. Three samples, TSH, free T4, haemoglobin, no fasting. I will wait for the form, I have not taken blood yet.
[SEG0050] person_2 (DOCTOR): Yes, take all three once the form is printed, TSH, free T4 and haemoglobin. Today itself, after we finish.

[SEG0051] person_3 (PATIENT): Will the report come today? I have a stock audit tomorrow, my manager is already sour that I left for the clinic, and the showroom sale starts, which is not your problem. I talk too much when I am nervous.
[SEG0052] person_2 (DOCTOR): Not the same day. Usually next day or the day after. Come back next week with whatever report is ready. That is a proper follow-up, not only if you feel worse.
[SEG0053] person_3 (PATIENT): Thursday is my half day, I can come Thursday. If the paper is late, do I still show up, or will your receptionist scold me for coming empty-handed?
[SEG0054] person_2 (DOCTOR): Come next week anyway. If the report is not in, we still talk, and we open it the moment it arrives. The visit is not cancelled.
[SEG0055] person_4 (CAREGIVER): I will bring her. I can search for the blue file again, though I know what was circled.

[SEG0056] person_3 (PATIENT): One more, sorry. My feet are the coldest when I sit long at the computer. And my sleep is broken, I wake at three and then I am counting invoices. Is that thyroid, or is it just this sale season sitting in my head?

[SEG0057] person_2 (DOCTOR): Broken sleep can travel with low mood and with thyroid trouble, and a sale season will poke it. I am not putting a separate sleep label on you today. Same blood tests. Keep the vitamin D at sixty thousand units once a month, and next time tell me straight if a sachet was missed.
[SEG0058] person_3 (PATIENT): I will mark the calendar, Geeta can tick it, she is better at that than I am. Thank you. I walked in sure this was only work and age, and maybe some of it still is.
[SEG0059] person_2 (DOCTOR): Some of it may be. We still check. Nurse will draw the blood when the form prints, and I will see you next week.

Dry skin examination was described as mild on the forearms.
